injury.doctorNotes: Specific injury is an LCL sprain, likely grade 1. Has been out of practice since the injury occured and is unlikely to see any more preseason game action. Should have enough time to heal before week 1. I am not moving him in my rankings unless there is a setback.

For those who wanted to know, the psoas is a large muscle in the lower back which flexes the hip. Will likely miss the August 15th preseason game but should be back at practice the following week. As of now, this all sounds like the team is just being extra cautious with their number 1 receiver as opposed to a real injury concern. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 30.

injury.injuryName: Elbow Dislocation, Hamtring Strain, PCL Sprain
injury.injuryDate: Week 2 Knee sprain, Week 7 Hamstring, Week 9 Elbow dislocation
injury.doctorNotes: No physical limitations. Full participant in training camp. Appears fully recovered.

injury.reinjuryRate: Low to moderate depending on severity
injury.doctorNotes: A season ending injury was feared initially but updated reports of an ankle sprain allow for a collective sigh of relief. Updated reports were cryptic, calling the sprain "more low than high" and that's good enough for me to treat it like a high ankle sprain. This will most likely cost him several games to begin the year (and possibly more), giving Mike Washington some increased snaps/production as the presumed lead back to start the year. I wouldn't consider Jeanty until the 2-3 turn at the earliest.

10 months would have been late August so was initially looking good to be ready for the start of the regular season. Cleanup in May adds 4-6 weeks to the return timeline which pushes it into Late Sept/October. Avoided the preseason PUP, and could beat the estimate which is the good news. Could still miss 1-3 games to start the year. Expect about a month of decreased snaps/lower efficiency whenever he does return. Estimated eventual return to pre-injury level ~80-90%.

Diagnosis of high ankle sprain contradicted Coach LaFleur's downplaying of the injury after the game. Likely to miss multiple weeks of the preseason and possibly all of it. Still has a chance to be ready for week 1 - but could easily miss several weeks to start the year since players returning before they are fully healed have a significantly higher reinjury risk. Tyler Allgeier is a viable late round pick and has a good chance for increased snaps/production to start the year.

Injured in week 1.Tough ask for anyone to play through a sprained PCL. Credit to him for trying and actually playing in 12 total games. No surgery needed, no current limitations. Appears to be fully recovered.

injury.reinjuryRate: ~40% over next 2 years (if he returns for week 1)
injury.doctorNotes: Fully cleared for training camp and is practicing without restrictions. Likely he sits out all preseason games. Returning to play less than 9 months from his surgery date would statistically increase his re-injury risk. Week 1 is less than 9 months after surgery...Maybe the team holds him back a week or two to get the reinjury odds a lot more in their favor. Either way, if his luck holds out, he certainly has the ability to pay off in a big way this year at his current ADP. You just need to decide if you can stomach the increased risk if he/the team are truly committed to having him start week 1.
No physical limitations. Full participant in training camp. Appears fully recovered.

Got an MRI following the injury which suggested a low grade injury. Those usually have a rapid recovery timeline and low recurrence rate. Barring any unforseen issues/setbacks, he should return in 1-2 weeks and his week 1 status shouldn't be affected - although I'll feel better about it once we see him able to practice.

Arthroscopic cleanup from 2024 LCL/hamstring procedure in Mid May – 4-8 week recovery. Medically cleared for training camp and participating in full team drills. Basically, this is a very likely not going to be an issue for 2026. My concern for him going forward has much more to do with potential off the field issues rather than anything medical.

injury.injuryName: Blood Clot/Pulmonary Embolism + Multiple Documented Concussions
injury.doctorNotes: Off the blood thinners and with a new 4 year extension, he is currently participating in training camp with full medical clearance and no restrictions.

Initial report was he'd miss "a little bit of time." Later updated to "about a month." Was able to return to practice doing individual drills in late August which is encouraging for his week 1 availability barring any setbacks. Reinjury rate is ~15-25%. Certainly has the talent to pay off in a big way in 2026 so I wouldn't fault anyone for rolling the dice on him - just make sure you understand the risk before using that high draft pick on him.
He'll miss some preseason time - but should be ready for week 1 barring any setbacks.

The August hamstring injury occurred weeks after his previous hamstring injury forced him to miss the final 2 weeks of June OTAs/minicamp. Still has enough time to get healthy for week 1, but the fact that he's already had a recurrence ups his reinjury risk profile, and the missed practice time increases the chances he starts the year off slowly. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 20

Sustained another hamstring injury in practice on August 13th. This throws a little bit of a wet blanket on the recent enthusiasm for him. Likely to be placed on short-term IR to start the year. Still has a high ceiling, but mind the reinjury risk (~30%) and how that and the projected missed time fits into your overall team build. UPDATE: Placed on IR on August 30 - will miss at least the first 4 games of the season.

MRI and projected timeline are suggestive of a grade 1 injury. Barring any setbacks, should be able to fully heal in time for week 1 - although mind the reinjury risk of ~15-25% when deciding if you want to pay up for him at his current ADP.
Full participant in training camp. No limitations. Appears fully recovered.
Contusion is a fancy word for "bruise." He probably will miss a few days of practice. Should be fine after that.

injury.injuryName: Left Foot Stress Reaction/Fracture; Right Leg Injury
injury.doctorNotes: Rome has walked back his previous comments about his foot structure feeling "different" post injury and reaffirms that his left foot feels "amazing" and has no pain. Of note, his more recent injury is to the opposite leg of his prior foot injury so it is not a recurrence. Early reports suggest that he "should be all good" and his week 1 status will not be affected. Coach Ben Johnson will address the media on this in the second week of September, but I'm not concerned/changing his ranking for now. One caveat to all this remains that if the pain in his LEFT foot returns, he becomes an AVOID due to the possibility of stress reaction recurrence.
Suspect this is a grade 1 injury. Barring any setbacks, he should have enough time to be fully healed by week 1. Reinjury rate ~30%. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 17

injury.injuryName: Left Shoulder Subluxation/Dislocation + Non Lisfranc mid foot sprain
injury.doctorNotes: Full participant in training camp. Appears fully recovered. Could pay off at his ADP, but note that he still carries some risk post surgery and will likely be competing for touches.

Removed from the PUP and returned to practice in a limited capacity at the end of July. 10 months post surgery would be just before week 1 – so I think he has a legitimate chance to be ready provided he has no setbacks/additional issues. Still expect ~4 weeks of decreased snaps/efficiency after he returns. Even with the current optimism, given the elevated risk and current timeline, it may still be better to pass unless you get a discount.

injury.injuryName: Right Tibia Fracture, Ankle Dislocation & Ruptured Deltoid Ligament
injury.doctorNotes: Full participant in training camp. Appears fully recovered.

injury.injuryName: Left practice with left leg "muscle tightness"
injury.doctorNotes: Left practice with what was initially called leg muscle tightness, later amended by Coach Payton to a “strain” (probably a low grade – quad, hamstring?). Expected back at practice in mid August. Should have enough time to be fully headed by week 1. Injury recurrence rate ~10-30% depending on actual body part injured. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 17

injury.injuryName: Herniated Disc in Lower Back/Hip Injury
injury.doctorNotes: High success rates for type of back surgery he had. Full participant since the start of training camp prior to recent injury. Hip injury could simply be a soft tissue bruise. Given the mechanism of injury could also be a hip pointer (bone bruise) - should have enough time to heal up for week 1.

The news of the setback is discouraging but he's still technically within the expected recovery timeline if he returns in August (and would still have ~2 weeks after that until week 1). Expect he’ll be ready for week 1 but, how much does missing all of the camp/practice time hurt him. Slow start? Mason Taylor bump?

Follow up reports stated Swift was simply dealing with a muscle cramp. He is expected to return to practice leading up to the Bears week 1 game and barring any additional bad news, this is likely much ado about nothing.

Began training camp on the PUP, no clear timetable for return. Should be fine once he is back and has several weeks to ramp up, but it's anyone's guess as to when that will be. For now buyer beware and I'm avoiding at his current ADP. UPDATE: Activated from the PUP on August 27.
No physical limitations. Full participant in training camp. Appears fully recovered.
Typical repair timeline is 6-9 months. He's practicing at training camp and reportedly looking good (on BOTH sides of the ball)! I’m optimistic all around.

Recent update from Coach LaFleur on 8/11 is that he will sit out "at least this week." Probably a grade 1 injury. If he's not back at practice within a couple of weeks, that raises the concern for a higher grade injury - which would put his week 1 status at risk. There is also the risk of a possible suspension being handed down by the league this year. NOTE: Returned to practice on August 18th. UPDATE: Placed on Commissioner's Exempt list on August 30. Don't draft until the double digit rounds, and maybe not at all.

Full participant in training camp. No limitations. Small sample size of players with this injury course but some studies estimate ~40-60% chance of return to pre-injury level. Younger players tended to do better, so I'd put his chances on the high end of that range.

9 months from the surgery would be mid October. He began training camp on the PUP but recently started running routes. Actual return date remains unclear. Team traveling to Australia for week 1, probably a coin flip he makes the trip. Team could hold him out until week 2 stateside, or be cautious and leave him on the PUP. Some studies have shown decreased performance for “skill” players coming back from Achillies repair can be up to 20-30%. Even with that kind of drop off – Kittle could still finish as a Top 6 TE on a PPG basis when he does return.

Expected back at practice in mid-August. As long as that happens and there are no setbacks, he should have enough time to be fully healed/recovered by week 1. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 11

injury.injuryName: Chronic Hamstring Strains/Left Quadriceps Injury x 2, groin injury
injury.doctorNotes: Recurrent hamstring injuries were the concern coming into 2026, but he picked up a quadriceps strain early in training camp and missed about 2 weeks before returning on 8/15 and suffered a recurrence several days later which cost him more time. Also suffered a groin injury in late August - likely a grade 1. Still likely for week 1 but these all up the risk for reinjury and/or a slow start to the year. Unless you can get at least a significant discount on his current ADP, I'd pass on drafting him for now.

injury.injuryName: Right Shoulder Dislocation & Torn Labrum in 2025, Scare in Camp
injury.reinjuryRate: ~10-20% with regard to his offseason shoulder surgery.
injury.doctorNotes: Higher concern given this is the same shoulder that was operated on in the offseason. Could be much ado about nothing. UPDATE: Returned to practice on August 10

The injury was described as "legit" by Coach Canales and he has already been labeled "week to week" as for his recovery. Both of those things speak to a more significant injury - I suspect this is a grade 2/partial tear. If that's the case, he's right at the range where he could be ready for week 1, but could also easily miss multiple weeks to start the season. Either way, if you thought the Jonathan Brooks rocket ship had reached cruising altitude, you'd better buckle up.

High rate of return to play post surgery approaching 90%. Return to pre-injury level ~60-80%. The delay between his initial injury and surgery lowers the likelihood of full return to pre-injury level - so I'd estimate his chances to eventually return to pre-injury form on the lower end of the range.
Recently returned to practice and should be fine for week 1 barring any additonal issues/setbacks.
Injury confirmed with MRI. Take him off your draft boards and check back in on him in the offseason.
"Soft tissue injury" quote comes from HC Sean Payton. UPDATE: returned to practice the following day. Nothing to see here.

Currently throwing at training camp but not yet cleared for full participation. Likely that he begins the year on PUP. Any setbacks could push recovery into October or November (or later). When he does return, chances he’ll get back to his pre-injury level are ~60-85%.

injury.reinjuryRate: ~20-25% over next 2 years (bump that to ~40% if he returns before mid November)
injury.doctorNotes: Currently on the PUP. 9 months post surgery is mid November which is essentially best case. More realistic return is early/mid December (~10 months). Any setbacks and he could miss even more of the regular season or maybe even the whole year. If he returns prior to mid-November, his re-injury risk over the next 2 years is ~40%.

The 2026 3rd round pick is likely to miss at least the first 4 games of the year. Even if he doesn't, will need about a month of ramp up (with associated decreased snap share and efficiency) when he does return. Justifiable dart throw late if you have the ability to stash on deep bench or IR slot.
Currently at training camp and participating in individual and team drills.

A bone bruise is when the inner part of the bone breaks but the outer portion is still intact. Can swell and are very painful. Small ones can heal in ~1-2 weeks, larger ones can take much longer. He was able to return to practice on Friday 8/7 and it looks like he dodged a bullet here.

Suspect this is a grade 1 MCL injury. The MCL has a relatively good blood supply compared to other structures in the knee which helps with the natural healing process. Should have enough time to get the knee healed up for week 1 barring any setbacks/other issues. The back issue is a different story; he's a hard avoid for me until we get more information and the injury specifics. UPDATE: Placed on IR on September 1.
High success rate (>90%) for surgical repair of LCL. Should be back in time for OTAs in 2027 if all goes well.

injury.reinjuryRate: Moderate - Especially if returning within 3 weeks
injury.doctorNotes: Provided injury timeline of him missing "at least a month" suggests a grade 2 injury. It's likely that he misses several games to begin the year and could be placed on short-term IR. I'd look elsewhere for my late round dart throw. His abscence bumps the early season projection for Travis Etienne Jr.

Currently not practicing. No return date yet, but could be back at practice within the next week to 10 days. Assuming a grade 1 injury, he should have enough time to fully heal before week 1. Any setbacks or confirmation of a more significant injury would put his week 1 availability in jeopardy.
Will miss some practice time, but should have enough time to heal up for week 1 barring any additional issues/setbacks.

Unbelievably, many athletes are able to return to play after this type of injury. Recent studies show high rates of return to pre-injury level (up to almost 90%) for younger athletes - unfortunately that doesn't apply for Hill at age 32. Given he was already showing signs of decline pre-injury, the chances that we ever see "vintage Cheetah" again are low.
Currently not practicing with no official return date. Should have enough time to get healed up before week 1.
Full participant in training camp as of August 1.

Week 1 is about 20 months post injury. He’s at training camp and avoided the preseason PUP, but is not cleared for full practices yet (Hopefully that happens by mid-August). Chance he returns to pre-injury level are between 50-80%. UPDATE: Placed on IR on August 30 - will miss at least the first 4 games of the season.
Currently participating in training camp, although he has not been fully cleared yet. UPDATE: Placed on IR on August 30 - will miss at least the first 4 games of the year.
